objective: Port netty-codec-dns (io.netty.handler.codec.dns (DNS message codec: records, queries, responses, TCP/UDP encoders and decoders)) with its original tests: Java names (case and the Async suffix may differ), the original structure and every original comment, and an explicit evidence-backed record for each CLR adaptation and each unit that is not ported.

ownerDecisions: Project, folder and assembly names are the namespace root of the module (owner decision 2026-11-19, see docs/codec-base-porting.md): each codec module takes the namespace of its main package, and the tests use <project>.Tests like the other test projects.

Owner decisions 2026-11-19 for the codec modules that only need codec-base: one project per Maven module; codec-socks is Netty.NET.Handler.Codec.Socks (its Maven and JPMS name) and holds the socks and socksx namespaces; haproxy is HAProxy (the casing of the Java types in that package); socksx, v4 and v5 are Socksx, V4 and V5.

statusMeaning.verified: Every declared original test is mapped to a C# test with the same name (case may differ) and passes.
statusMeaning.clr-adapted: Ported with the original names, structure and comments; every CLR difference is stated in a // CLR: comment and in this entry. For tests, some original methods are CLR-inapplicable with recorded evidence.
statusMeaning.deprecated-not-ported: @Deprecated Java unit (or a helper serving one) that is not ported; the deprecation facts, reason, replacement and every original comment/test are recorded.

review.scope: Non-final methods are virtual; the narrowed retain()/retain(int)/touch()/touch(Object) are C# 9 covariant overrides of the virtual AbstractReferenceCounted members of Common. The leak tracker is created first in the constructor because a C# instance field initializer cannot reference the instance being created (C# specification 15.5.6.3). Records are List<IDnsRecord>; List.set/remove return values are read before the indexer write/RemoveAt. A source IndexOutOfBoundsException is ArgumentOutOfRangeException(null, source text) and java.lang.Error for an impossible section number is UnreachableException (as codec-base's LengthFieldPrepender). The erased unchecked cast of castRecord is a checked C# cast (InvalidCastException at the call for a mismatched T). checkQuestion names IDnsQuestion (the CLR simple name) in its message; checkNotNull(section) has no counterpart because a C# enum value cannot be null; assert is Debug.Assert. Numbers in text and messages use the invariant culture (Int32.ToString() otherwise uses the current culture).

Source bit packing; the package-private final toStringBuilder() is internal and non-virtual; the (int) and (short) narrowings are unchecked. Numbers in text and messages use the invariant culture (Int32.ToString() otherwise uses the current culture).

Accessors stay virtual methods. IDN.toASCII(name) is the shared Netty.NET.Common.Internal.IDN.ToASCII (owner decision 2026-11-19, shared with codec-socks), which keeps the OpenJDK label loop (root label ".", "" stays "", ASCII labels unchanged, empty-label and 63-character checks) and passes only non-ASCII labels to IdnMapping; failures are ArgumentException. equalsIgnoreCase is StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase; hashCode() uses ToLowerInvariant (Java toLowerCase() uses the default locale) and string.GetHashCode(), which differs from the Java String.hashCode() value and between runs but is equal for equal names. The (short) dnsClass narrowing is unchecked. Numbers in text and messages use the invariant culture (Int32.ToString() otherwise uses the current culture).

AddressedEnvelope<M, InetSocketAddress> is the Transport IAddressedEnvelope<M, IPEndPoint>, whose content(), sender() and recipient() are the Content, Sender and Recipient properties of that port; AddressedEnvelope<?, SocketAddress> in equals() is IAddressedEnvelope<object, EndPoint>, which the covariant out parameters match for every reference content type. The Java overrides that narrow the return type are C# 9 covariant overrides ("an overriding method can declare a more derived return type", Microsoft Learn, Covariance and Contravariance in Generics). The NullPointerException for two null addresses is ArgumentNullException, as in DefaultAddressedEnvelope.

Interface with the I prefix over IReferenceCounted. <T extends DnsRecord> T recordAt/setRecord/removeRecord keep the type parameter as T : IDnsRecord; Java infers T from the assignment, C# only from arguments ("it cannot infer the type parameters only from a constraint or return value", Microsoft Learn), so callers write RecordAt<IDnsQuestion>(section). The Java re-declarations that only narrow a return type are inherited unchanged from the base interface, the Transport/Common rule "C# 9 covariant returns cover class overrides only" (docs/transport-porting.md); the implementing classes keep the narrowed return types. (touch/retain re-declarations).

The package-private final utility class is an internal static class; the nested DnsQueryFactory is the internal interface IDnsQueryFactory. An AddressedEnvelope check is IAddressedEnvelope<object, EndPoint>; an address is printed by EndPoint.ToString() ("192.168.1.2:80" for IPEndPoint) instead of Java's InetSocketAddress.toString() ("host/literal:port"), as in Transport's DefaultAddressedEnvelope.ToString(). setCharAt is the StringBuilder indexer. Numbers in text and messages use the invariant culture (Int32.ToString() otherwise uses the current culture).

Value class with static readonly constants; Comparable is IComparable<DnsOpCode>. The Java byte opcode is the unsigned System.Byte (owner rule for ByteBuf bytes), so the sign-dependent results keep the Java value through an sbyte reinterpretation: hashCode() returns the signed byte widened to int and compareTo() subtracts the signed bytes (opcodes 128..255 hash negative and sort first, as in Java). toString() uses byteValue & 0xFF, the unsigned value itself. The (byte) narrowing of the constructor is unchecked. Numbers in text and messages use the invariant culture (Int32.ToString() otherwise uses the current culture).
